title: Wonders in the modern age
summary: Why enchanted objects still matter to mages.

claims.text: Many mages assume Wonders are outdated, since they are rare, slow to make, and a glowing sword in the street invites Paradox.
Yet Sleepers more readily believe that magic comes from magical things, or from high technology, than from magical people.
A Wonder does not spare its user from Paradox, but it can blunt the extra backlash that hostile witnesses bring.
An Artifact holds lasting magical Effects that an Awakened user can call on; its technomagic counterpart is an Invention.
A Charm gives one short burst of power until its material is spent, such as a candle burned down or a bullet fired; Technocrats call such things Gadgets.
A Fetish houses a spirit, a Familiar is a spirit with a lasting body bonded to a mage, and a Periapt is a refillable store of Quintessence.
A Talisman holds its own Arete and a sliver of its maker's will, so it may act on its own, sometimes to its owner's cost.

title: Grimoires
summary: Books that hold a piece of Enlightened will.

claims.text: A Grimoire is a book or other store of data, written with rare skill and infused with its maker's will, that can deepen an Awakened reader's grasp of reality.
It must be read whole and in its own language, so most Grimoires sit in Hermetic libraries, where the love of languages runs deep.
Countless Grimoires were lost with Horizon, though some insist its librarian Nicodemus Mulhouse had wards ready to carry the library to safety.
